analysis.title: GS Basics - Supportive Micro. Deposit Competition. Downside Growth Risk
key_insights: Overnight US rebound carried into the broader tech tape: Hynix +5%, Samsung +4%, KOSPI +3%. Privorotsky asks whether it is an oversold bounce in QQQ or the start of something more sustainable.

Heading into major political events next week with substantial risk premium already embedded, the desk says markets tend to be constructive: the market struggles to go down even though people remain reluctant to add risk.

Gulf diplomacy is active (Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani delegations in Tehran, Qatar mediating) but nothing substantive. The odds of a breakthrough remain low. Oil has come off Friday's escalatory highs.

If there is no tangible progress by Thursday morning, the desk expects a climb up the escalatory ladder into the weekend again, though the market will stay skeptical that much happens ahead of next week's political events.

HSBC fell 5.6% in Hong Kong, setting a difficult tone for banks. Increased deposit competition in the UK and Hong Kong contributed to net interest income (NII) compression, and the desk flags Europe more broadly as exposed to deposit competition and a lingering threat from agentic capital allocation.

Neoclouds were under pressure after Elon's comments on financing and consolidation. AI credit spreads came off Friday's wides, but credit remains the most important thing to watch. The key issue is the market's willingness to supply capital and at what price.

The desk raises the possibility that the scale of AI spending eventually drives compute overcapacity into 2027/28, structurally lower returns and lower multiples, but calls this unclear. What is clear is that the cost of capital has risen materially, changing the economics of the whole complex. Any sustained credit relief would be a powerful catalyst.

Micro remains robust: Celestica rose about 17% aftermarket after a comfortable beat and guidance of $40bn revenue in 2027, up 90% YoY, with 2028 demand indications stronger. Cadence beat and raised with $8.2bn of backlog. Rambus beat but slipped after the close. The debate is how much to discount future cash flows given supply, competition and financing uncertainty.

Front-end rates have stabilized, which the desk calls good for risk. Elevated energy is more likely to produce chop than a sustained selloff absent escalation. Credit is still flashing yellow to red relative to equities, and calming in credit could catalyze a broader rally.

Hyperscaler earnings and the Fed are this week's main event. The desk focuses on capex (flat or up is fine, down would be disastrous for picks-and-shovels names), backlog conversion to revenue, free cash flow in out quarters, and financing (equity versus debt).

Flows were more supportive: after weeks as net sellers of tech, the desk saw client demand on the other side, at least in Europe. The modal view is to chop around until next week's political events clear.
